the design of new chiral stationary phases based on macrocyclic receptors and the application of the resulting phases to the study of enantioselectivity in solution.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of macrocyclic synthetic hosts and macrocyclic natural products for the design of chiral HPLC stationary phases represents an innovative and successful approach to the enantioseparation of organic compounds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
macrocyclic hosts can be successfully grafted onto silica and used as HPLC chiroselective phases.
macrocyclic synthetic receptors and the macrocyclic glycopetides can be used as effective chiral selectors in the enantioseparations of a wide variety of chiral compounds.

, in the last few years, the design of new chiral HPLC stationary phases, which is based on the use of macrocyclic synthetic receptors or macrocyclic glycoamino acid-based receptors, is a very promising and fruitful field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic and natural macrocyclic receptors can be successfully grafted on silica supports and used as chiral stationary phases in enantiospecific HPLC.
HPLC chiroptical stationary phases based on synthetic receptors and glycopeptide natural receptors have a high potential for applications in the field of chiral recognition.

the immobilization of natural or synthetic receptors on solid supports allows the design of innovative chiral phases that are able to recognize a wide range of chiral analytes, thus opening up new perspectives for the enantiomeric analysis of compounds that cannot be separated with existing chiral stationary phases.
